assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed how trade is modelled and measured. It reoriented empirical work on micro data and the welfare analysis of trade. The Melitz framework is a workhorse in trade, IO and macro, and it complements rather than repeats the 2008 recognition of new trade theory.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman is a core co-developer through Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple and related work. Redding is influential on the quantitative and spatial side but is later and more derivative. The empirical firm-level foundations from other authors (for example Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum), who are not on the credited list, are a real attribution gap. Helpman also appears in B001, so the Committee would have to decide which of his bodies of work is being recognised.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation across countries, data sets and subfields. Timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers a narrower award that includes the empirical firm-level pioneers.
Overlap with Helpman's other work in B001.
My knowledge of the detailed priority claims is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression extended econometrics beyond conditional means. It is now standard for distributional questions in labour, inequality, finance and risk. The method is general and has become routine across applied fields, which is the kind of broad methodological reach the prize has recognised before.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett (1978) introduced the estimator, and Koenker's later theory, computation and monograph consolidated it. Chernozhukov is credited for later inference and high-dimensional extensions. These are important but are a later, partly separate contribution that also appears in B007, so I leave him off this ballot.
assessment.maturity: Over 45 years of use and extensions. Priority is clear and the method is thoroughly confirmed.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee treats the contribution as sufficiently economic rather than statistical.
Whether Chernozhukov's extensions should be credited here.
Age and health of the earliest contributors are not assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Credit cycles, collateral constraints and amplification explain why small shocks can have large and persistent real effects. The mechanism became central to macro-finance and to post-2008 policy thinking. The 2022 prize recognised banks and financial crises, but the collateral-constraint amplification mechanism is a distinct theoretical contribution.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) is the core paper and is clearly identifiable. Gertler and Gilchrist developed the financial accelerator and its empirical side, and Gertler also appears in B038. I would credit the two originators of the collateral mechanism and leave the accelerator authors out, though that boundary is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of influence, with extensive follow-on work including macroprudential and quantitative applications.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 award (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig) and with the financial accelerator literature.
How much weight the Committee gives to a single seminal paper versus an empirical research programme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Estimation of differentiated-product demand with endogenous prices, together with dynamic industry models, made empirical IO usable for merger analysis, antitrust and welfare measurement. It has influenced policy practice and spread to trade, health and environmental economics.
assessment.attribution: Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes (1995) and Berry (1994) are the central contributions, with Pakes also behind the dynamic models and the Ericson-Pakes framework. Bresnahan's earlier work on the same question is an important antecedent that the three-name limit may cut out. The list of seven credited names shows diffuse credit across the field.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of widespread use, including in regulatory practice. Strongly confirmed.
uncertainties: Whether Bresnahan's priority claim should displace one of the three names.
The line between methodological innovation and applied implementation is hard to draw here.
Sensitivity of results to functional-form and instrument assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. Staggered pricing, interest-rate rules and the microfounded policy framework have shaped how inflation and stabilisation are modelled and conducted.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across eight named people, which makes an award hard. Calvo's pricing device, Taylor's staggered contracts and rule, and Woodford's synthesis are the most identifiable conceptual contributions. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are important for estimation and extension, and a three-person limit leaves out much of the empirical DSGE work.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use in policy. The framework has been challenged and modified since 2008 and the pandemic inflation, which is a point of both test and refinement.
uncertainties: Severe attribution diffusion and the three-laureate cap.
Debate over how well the framework performed in recent inflation episodes.
Overlap with prior macro prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work on how technology and trade shocks reshape labour demand and wages, including the China shock evidence on local adjustment, changed the policy debate on globalisation and inequality. The empirical designs are widely emulated and the findings overturned the assumption of fast adjustment.
assessment.attribution: Autor's task-based work and the China-shock papers with Dorn and Hanson are the central contributions. Katz (also in B014) is credited for the education-technology race. The task-framework antecedents of Levy and Murnane are not on the list. Acemoglu's 2024 prize adds some overlap on technology and labour.
assessment.maturity: The main findings date from 2013 onward and have been extensively replicated and debated, with the interpretation of long-run effects still evolving.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 award and with the 2021 recognition of empirical labour methods.
Contested persistence and magnitude of the effects.
Which of Dorn and Katz should be credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Administrative data used at population scale transformed measurement of opportunity, mobility and neighbourhood effects, with direct policy influence. The methodological and measurement contribution is substantial, and Chetty's broader public-economics work adds weight.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are the clearest leaders on the neighbourhood and mobility papers. Friedman and Katz are important co-authors, and Katz's Moving to Opportunity work predates the others. The large collaborative structure complicates the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: The core results are about a decade old. Replication and debate over causal interpretation and measurement are ongoing, so confirmation is shorter than for the other candidates.
uncertainties: Younger work with less time for settled consensus.
Debate over mobility estimates and the role of place.
Division of credit among a large team.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their political-economy models of trade protection (the 'protection for sale' framework) gave a tractable micro-political account of why trade policy deviates from efficiency. Their joint work on endogenous growth and trade also broadened the field. The influence is large in trade and in political economy.
assessment.attribution: Credit to Grossman and Helpman is clear and joint, covering lobbying and protection as well as innovation and growth. Helpman's overlap with B020 means the Committee would face a choice or a combined award.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation. The theory has been tested less directly than the heterogeneous-firm models, though it remains the standard reference framework.
uncertainties: Empirical support for the protection-for-sale predictions is mixed.
Overlap with B020 on Helpman.
Whether the Committee sees the contribution as primarily theory with limited measurement.
